item.text: {"question_id":"2B.9","answer":"During 2023, the Tshisekedi administration supported several accountability and remedy mechanisms, but the evidence shows stronger formal commitment than consistently effective implementation. The government invited an ICC investigation into alleged RDF/M23 crimes, signed a cooperation agreement facilitating ICC activity, and Tshisekedi publicly endorsed rule-of-law and proposed judicial, special-court, and victim-reparation mechanisms; these actions primarily addressed alleged abuses by opposing forces and do not establish acceptance of responsibility for Congolese conduct or completed remedies (BATCH-0005-E001; BATCH-0019-E001; BATCH-0019-E002; BATCH-0015-E003). The government also promulgated a victim-protection and reparation framework, established an inquiry into alleged FARDC violence in Goma and Kwamouth, and reported military training, ethics commitments, and institutional measures intended to reduce abuse (BATCH-0029-E001; BATCH-0029-E002; BATCH-0011-E003; BATCH-0011-E004). There was some domestic accountability: courts prosecuted security personnel for Kwamouth abuses, including death and prison sentences, and in the Goma case authorities arrested and tried security personnel; one commander was convicted and dismissed, three soldiers imprisoned, and a court ordered reparations to recognized victims (BATCH-0011-E002; BATCH-0011-E021). However, these proceedings were institutionally conducted rather than personally directed by Tshisekedi, and the Goma investigations and trials had serious deficiencies: disputed casualty counts, absent ballistic investigations and autopsies, incomplete identification and disclosure of victims, restricted victim participation, and limited reparations. Authorities also prosecuted many civilians in proceedings Amnesty considered inadequately individualized, while most serious atrocities remained unpunished and transitional-justice commitments lacked concrete implementation (BATCH-0011-E020; BATCH-0011-E021; BATCH-0010-E016; BATCH-0028-E018). Government monitoring cooperation was partial: some domestic and international monitoring was permitted, but access to certain military and intelligence detention facilities was denied and institutional bodies struggled with effectiveness (BATCH-0011-E014). Tshisekedi acknowledged justice-system shortcomings, and his stated non-intervention in a journalist’s case is consistent with respect for separation of powers, but neither fact demonstrates comprehensive responsibility-taking or remedy (BATCH-0028-E018; BATCH-0025-E013). Overall, the period shows meaningful formal cooperation, some prosecutions, discipline, and legal remedy design, alongside incomplete accountability, contested casualty disclosure, weak implementation, and limited evidence that the president personally accepted responsibility or ensured effective remedy.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0019-E001","BATCH-0019-E002","BATCH-0015-E003","BATCH-0029-E001","BATCH-0029-E002","BATCH-0011-E003","BATCH-0011-E004","BATCH-0011-E002","BATCH-0011-E021","BATCH-0025-E013"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E001","BATCH-0010-E016","BATCH-0011-E014","BATCH-0011-E020","BATCH-0011-E021","BATCH-0028-E018","BATCH-0023-E014"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not establish Tshisekedi’s personal direction of individual prosecutions, military decisions, investigations, or reparations.","ICC cooperation, legal frameworks, inquiries, and presidential proposals are not shown to have produced completed outcomes during the period.","Casualty totals and responsibility for the Goma events remained contested; investigations lacked ballistic work, autopsies, complete victim identification, and full disclosure.","The evidence does not establish that the victim fund was staffed, funded, or delivering reparations in 2023.","Domestic prosecutions and convictions provide evidence of some accountability but do not demonstrate consistent discipline of senior actors or comprehensive remedy.","The evidence concerns 2023; later reporting is used only to assess the status or implementation of 2023 commitments, not to infer outcomes beyond the supplied record."],"corrections_made":["Reclassified ICC referrals and cooperation as accountability-seeking actions focused mainly on alleged RDF/M23 abuses, rather than proof that Tshisekedi accepted responsibility for Congolese abuses.","Added the omitted domestic prosecutions, security-force convictions, commander dismissal, and Goma reparations order.","Separated government and military-institution conduct from personally established presidential responsibility.","Qualified formal victim-reparation laws, inquiries, training, and presidential proposals as design or stated commitments without demonstrated implementation.","Preserved contrary evidence concerning incomplete investigations, disputed casualty disclosure, restricted access, flawed proceedings, and continuing impunity.","Removed unsupported claims about calls for sanctions, UN/AU engagement, or public acknowledgement of individual justice failures where the supplied passages did not directly support the intended characterization."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Final outcomes of the ICC cooperation and requested investigations are not supplied.","Implementation, funding, staffing, and disbursement records for the victim-reparation fund are absent.","Further evidence could clarify whether Tshisekedi directed, monitored, or corrected the Goma accountability process and whether senior commanders faced meaningful discipline.","A complete casualty-disclosure record and later appellate outcomes could materially change the assessment of transparency and remedy."]}
